tiers.reinforcement: Additional exercises at the same conceptual level.
tiers.extension: Concept material not required by the primary spine.
tiers.stretch: Higher-complexity integration after the stage core.

stages.name: Orientation and feedback loop
outcomes: Run one exercise and its tests locally.
Read failures as executable specifications.
Use names, calls, returns, and basic type annotations.

stages.name: Scalar types, expressions, and control flow
outcomes: Model booleans and numeric values.
Compose comparisons and conditional branches.
Recognize representation-level numeric operations.

stages.name: Strings and text processing
outcomes: Transform, split, normalize, and format text.
Distinguish Unicode text from byte-oriented data.
Build small parsing pipelines without premature regex use.

stages.name: Sequences, iteration, and generators
outcomes: Choose lists, tuples, and general sequence operations.
Write explicit loops before compressing them.
Use iterators and generators for incremental production.

stages.name: Mappings, sets, and comprehensions
outcomes: Model lookup, membership, counting, and grouping.
Use comprehensions when they preserve readability.
Select collection semantics before selecting syntax.

stages.name: Functions and functional composition
outcomes: Design narrow functions with explicit contracts.
Use argument forms and higher-order functions deliberately.
Separate transformation, filtering, and orchestration.

stages.name: Exceptions and resource boundaries
outcomes: Raise domain-specific failures at contract boundaries.
Handle only errors a layer can resolve.
Use context managers for deterministic cleanup.

stages.name: Classes and domain modeling
outcomes: Use classes where state and invariants belong together.
Prefer composition before inheritance.
Represent finite states with enums and data-oriented classes.

stages.name: Protocols and Python idioms
outcomes: Implement iteration, comparison, and operator protocols.
Understand descriptors, decorators, and customization hooks.
Use typing and interfaces as contract surfaces.

stages.name: Standard-library problem solving
outcomes: Use datetime, regex, random, itertools, functools, and collections.
Prefer a standard abstraction over hand-rolled machinery.
Keep library adapters at explicit boundaries.

stages.name: Recursion and smaller data structures and algorithms
outcomes: State invariants for search and traversal.
Implement stacks, queues, linked structures, and trees.
Compare iterative, recursive, greedy, and dynamic approaches.

stages.name: Integrated capstones
outcomes: Decompose multi-rule systems into testable components.
Control state-space growth and isolate side effects.
Refactor only after a correct observable baseline exists.
